description: This file defines the class HTMLPurifier_DefinitionCache_Serializer, which manages serialization-based caching of definitions for the HTMLPurifier library. It includes methods for adding, setting, replacing, retrieving, removing, and cleaning cache files, as well as generating file paths and handling directory permissions.

classes.name: HTMLPurifier_DefinitionCache_Serializer
classes.description: A class that handles serialization caching for HTMLPurifier definitions, including file operations such as write, read, delete, and directory management.

methods.name: add
methods.description: Adds a serialized definition to the cache, creating a file unless it already exists.

methods.name: set
methods.description: Sets a serialized definition in the cache, overwriting existing files.

methods.name: replace
methods.description: Replaces an existing cache file with a new serialized definition.

methods.name: get
methods.description: Retrieves and unserializes a cached definition based on the current configuration.

methods.name: remove
methods.description: Removes the cache file associated with the configuration.

methods.name: flush
methods.description: Deletes all cache files in the cache directory.

methods.name: cleanup
methods.description: Removes old cache files based on their age or criteria specified.

methods.name: generateFilePath
methods.description: Generates the full file path for the cache file based on the configuration.

methods.name: generateDirectoryPath
methods.description: Generates the directory path where cache files are stored.

methods.name: generateBaseDirectoryPath
methods.description: Generates the base directory path where all cache serials are stored, defaulting to a specific prefix if not set in configuration.

methods.name: _write
methods.description: Internal method for writing serialized data to a file, including setting permissions.

methods.name: _prepareDir
methods.description: Internal method to ensure the cache directory exists with proper permissions.

methods.name: _testPermissions
methods.description: Checks if a directory has writable permissions, attempting to fix permissions if possible.
